items.heading: Language focus: contract language
items.paragraph:
Contracts use formal, fixed patterns:

shall = must (an obligation): The contractor shall complete the works by 30 June.

shall not = must not: The contractor shall not start varied work without an instruction.

is entitled to = has the right to: The employer is entitled to hold 5% retention.

is responsible for + noun / -ing: The contractor is responsible for repairing defects.

To quote the contract, name the clause: Under clause 8.7, liquidated damages are 2,000 dollars per day.
Careful: shall in a contract is not polite or old-fashioned – it creates a legal duty. In meetings, say must or has to; in the contract text, keep shall.

items.heading: Language focus: describing and pricing a change
items.paragraph:
Describing the change: add a canopy · omit the planters · replace painted steel with stainless steel · increase the width from 2.0 to 2.5 metres.

Pricing with would (the change is not agreed yet): The canopy would cost 3,360 dollars and would take five working days.

After it is instructed and agreed, use will: The canopy will be installed in week 25.

Structure of a price: materials + labour = subtotal · subtotal + mark-up = total.
Careful: an omission reduces the price – but you may still claim time or cost already spent. Always check what has been ordered or built before you accept an omission.

items.heading: Language focus: the payment cycle in the passive
items.paragraph:
The cycle has fixed verbs, usually in the passive:

The application was submitted on the 25th. → 580,000 dollars has been certified. → Retention has been deducted. → Payment is due within 28 days. → The retention will be released at taking over.

Querying politely: Could you clarify why the daywork has not been certified? · We note that 20,000 dollars has been deducted…

Never accuse: not 'you cut our money', but 'the certified amount is 20,000 dollars lower than applied'.
Careful: due has two uses – the payment is due on 6 July (deadline) and the delay was due to late steel (cause). Context tells you which.

data.title: Notice of delay – Tower Crane 2 breakdown
data.glossNote: Read in English. Use the glossary above if you need help.
paras: Dear Sirs, under clause 20.1 of the contract we give notice of a delay event.

On Thursday 4 June at 11:15, Tower Crane 2 stopped because of a hoist motor fault. The replacement motor arrived from Almaty on Monday 8 June, and lifting restarted on Tuesday 9 June. Four working days were lost.
The lifting of the roof trusses is on the critical path. As a result, the works have been delayed by four working days, and we will apply for an extension of time to Monday 6 July.

As mitigation, we have moved two roofing teams to Block A and will work this Saturday. We will submit the full claim, with the crane log and the programme analysis, within 14 days. This notice is given without prejudice to our other rights under the contract.

The crane was repaired with a local motor.
How many working days were lost?
Why does the delay move the completion date?
opts: The trusses are on the critical path.

qs.q: What will be submitted within 14 days?
opts: The full claim with records and analysis

data.end: Well done! A notice answers: what happened, when, the effect, the mitigation, and what follows.

items.heading: Language focus: cause, effect and time
items.paragraph:
Cause: The works were delayed by the crane breakdown. · The delay was due to a hoist motor fault. · Four days were lost because of the fault.

Effect: As a result, the trusses are four days late. · The breakdown caused a four-day delay.

Critical path logic: The delay is on the critical path, so the completion date moves. · The painting has ten days of float, so a six-day delay there changes nothing.

Deadlines: within 14 days of the event · notice was given on 5 June.
Careful: an EOT moves the completion date – it does not pay your costs. Money is a separate claim. And acceleration (recovering time) is usually only paid if it was instructed.

items.fb: Critical delay − float = 4 days of EOT.

items.fb: The float absorbs it: zero. No EOT for the paint.

items.fb: 1, 2, 3 and 6 July – the revised date is Monday 6 July.

data.end: Tip: critical path + float decide the date; records decide the claim.

opts.fb: Facts, the contract, and the good news for him.
Arguing fault without facts convinces nobody.
Quote the contract and the facts.

opts.fb: Records answer doubt better than words.
Clients trust records, not promises.
Offer the documents.

opts.t: The extension itself only moves the date. We are not claiming acceleration costs, because we chose to recover the time ourselves.
opts.fb: You separate time from money clearly.

opts.t: We'll send a big claim later.
opts.fb: Vague threats destroy trust.

steps.say: Fine. What do you need from me?

opts.t: Nothing for the extension – it is granted. But please tell your director the handover date remains Tuesday, 30 June.
opts.fb: Clear close with the key message for the director.
Unprofessional.
If nothing is needed, say so clearly.

data.h: Testing and commissioning: proving the building works
hook: Commissioning week starts on Monday 15 June. Every system in Block B – water, power, ventilation, fire alarm, lifts – must prove that it works, with the consultant watching.
The results go into test certificates, and without those certificates there is no taking-over. This week, exact English matters: a test is passed, failed, or repeated – never 'more or less OK'.

terms.ex: Pressure testing of the pipework starts on Monday.
Commissioning proves that each system works as designed.
The consultant attends every witness test.
The functional test checks that the system does its job.
The performance test measures the real airflow.
The design value for the AHU is 4,500 cubic metres per hour.
The tolerance on airflow is plus or minus 10 per cent.
Each passed test gets a signed test certificate.

Balancing adjusts the airflow to every room.
In the cause-and-effect test, each alarm must stop the right fans.
Mr Hart witnessed the test and signed it off.

intro: Read the plan for commissioning week.
data.title: Commissioning programme – Block B, week of 15 June
data.glossNote: Read in English. Use the glossary above if you need help.
paras: Monday: flushing and filling of the heating and chilled water systems is completed, and the pumps are run for the first time. No witness required.
Tuesday: performance test of the air handling unit, witnessed by the consultant. The measured airflow must be within plus or minus 10 per cent of the design value of 4,500 cubic metres per hour.
Wednesday: balancing of the fan coil units, floor by floor. Thursday: lift load tests, witnessed by the inspection body, and the hot water performance test.

Friday: fire alarm cause-and-effect test. All fans must stop and the smoke dampers must close within 30 seconds of each alarm. Any failed test is repeated on Saturday morning. Signed test certificates are collected in the commissioning file, which is part of the handover documents.

qs.q: The AHU test is witnessed by the consultant.
A failed test ends the commissioning week.
What is the design airflow of the AHU?
Within how many seconds must the dampers close?
Where do the signed certificates go?
opts: Into the commissioning file for handover

data.end: Well done! is completed · witnessed by · must be within · is repeated – commissioning English.

items.heading: Language focus: sequences and conditions
items.paragraph:
Test sequences use time words with the present tense:

Once the system is flushed, we fill it with treated water. · We run the pump until the pressure is stable. · Before the consultant arrives, we check the instruments. · After each test passes, the certificate is signed.

Results against design: The measured value is 4,350 – within tolerance. · 4,000 is out of tolerance – the test is failed and repeated.

Status with the present perfect passive: The pipework has been flushed and tested. The AHU has not yet been balanced.
Careful: never sign a test certificate for a result you did not see. A certificate is evidence for 12 months of the defects liability period – and longer.

intro: Listen and calculate. Write numbers only.

items.say: The design airflow is four thousand five hundred cubic metres per hour, and the tolerance is plus or minus ten per cent. What is the minimum acceptable airflow?
And the maximum acceptable airflow?
The measured airflow is four thousand three hundred and fifty. Is it within tolerance? Answer with the measured number.
items.fb: 4,350 is between 4,050 and 4,950 – within tolerance, the test is passed.

items.say: The pipework is pressure-tested at six bar for thirty minutes. The allowed drop is zero point two bar. The gauge fell from six point zero to five point nine. How big was the drop?
items.fb: 0.1 bar – less than 0.2, the test is passed.

items.say: The smoke damper closed eighteen seconds after the alarm. The limit is thirty seconds. How many seconds of margin is that?

items.q: The AHU measures 4,000 against a minimum of 4,050. What do you report?
opts: The test is failed: 4,000 is below the minimum of 4,050. We will adjust and retest.
items.fb: Out of tolerance = failed, adjusted, retested. Never rounded up.

data.end: Tip: report the measured value, the limits and the verdict – in that order.

Thank you. I'll complete the certificate now – could you sign it before you leave the plant room?

steps.say: Fine. Please record the failure properly.

opts.t: Let's not write the failure down.
